key_insight: PMA tackles a neglected source of continual-learning failure in MLLMs: the projector itself forgets, so the model expands projector experts only when multimodal shifts demand it while keeping the pretrained projector as an anchor.
engineering_relevance: For computational science and engineering workflows that rely on multimodal models, PMA offers a practical way to preserve prior visual-language alignment across evolving datasets and instructions without retraining the whole model.
method: Detect multimodal distribution shifts with a lightweight representation descriptor.
Progressively expand projector experts only when needed and route inputs with an expandable multimodal router.
Retain the original pretrained projector as a stable alignment anchor to balance plasticity and stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on two recent MCIT benchmarks, with consistent gains over prior state-of-the-art methods and good transfer across diverse MLLM backbones.
watch_item: Because PMA adds expert expansion and routing logic, its benefit may depend on reliable shift detection and careful control of parameter growth and routing overhead.
paper_title: Progressive Multimodal Alignment for Continual Instruction Tuning
